scope.persona: A business settings user who needs confirmation after selecting Save, including when using assistive technology.

journeys.name: Save business settings and receive accessible, specific feedback

permittedActions: Inspect and modify files only under tests/forward/fix-fixture
Run the fixture's local Python test
prohibitedExternalEffects: Network access or requests to external systems
Changes outside the authorized fixture directory

claims.statement: Before the fix, the deterministic save-feedback contract failed because the status semantics and specific result text were absent.
After the fix, the fixture's deterministic save-feedback contract passes.
The Save handler now writes a specific local-only result into an element with role=status.
Actual browser rendering, keyboard behavior, and screen-reader announcement were not exercised in this source-contract retest.

evidence.summary: One test ran and failed because app.html did not contain id=save-result with role=status; the page also lacked the required specific save result.
The result paragraph has role=status, and the Save click handler assigns the exact text 'Saved locally. No external records were changed.' to that paragraph.

findings.title: Resolved: Save action did not expose accessible, specific feedback
findings.userImpact: Before the fix, selecting Save produced no visible or assistive-technology status, so users could not tell whether anything changed or whether external records were affected.
findings.rootCause: The result paragraph had no live status semantics, and the Save click handler was empty, leaving the feedback contract unimplemented.

recommendation.location: app.html, save result element and Save click handler
recommendation.recommendedChange: Add role=status to #save-result and set its text on Save to 'Saved locally. No external records were changed.'; preserve the existing contract test.
recommendation.alternative: Use an aria-live=polite feedback region with equivalent specific copy and extend the regression test to assert that implementation.
recommendation.tradeoffs: role=status is the smaller semantic change and implies polite live-region behavior; explicit aria-live offers more control but adds markup and test maintenance.

findings.retest: From the unchanged fixture source, run python test_app.py; pass requires one successful test, and any missing status role or exact feedback copy is a failure.

limitations: The retest validates the source feedback contract only; it does not prove browser or screen-reader behavior.
Business-name persistence behavior is outside this fixture test and was not evaluated.
untestedAreas: Rendered visual feedback in a real browser
Keyboard focus and screen-reader announcement behavior
Persistence or reload behavior for the business name
